decisions.statement: A specifier opening with a dot and a slash is refused.
A specifier climbing to a parent folder is refused.
A specifier spelled from the root package is let through.
A specifier naming a package is let through.
A specifier is read from the parse rather than from the text.
A string naming no module is let through.
A refusal names the specifier the body spells.
A refusal is filed at the body spelling the specifier.
One body spelling several relative paths is refused once for each.
A body is parsed only where its text spells a quote before a dot and a slash.
The scan deciding whether to parse reads the text rather than the parse.
A body that is not code is passed over.
Whether the file a specifier names is there is not read here.
A specifier written into a page's prose is not read here.
A `./+types/` specifier is resolved by tsconfig rootDirs, so it cannot be spelled from the root.

definition: the check refusing a specifier naming a file by a relative path
